newsitem.title: USA: U.S. copper consumers calm amid storming prices.
newsitem.headline: U.S. copper consumers calm amid storming prices.

text.p: Although U.S. copper consumer stocks are down to low levels to avoid year-end inventory tax, there were few signs of panic buying as prices storm ahead and LME copper hoards continue to shrink, traders said.
"If you see any panic buying, it would be because somebody is late with shipments and they don't have inventory," a broker said. "We are not seeing any real fundamental follow through to this."
COMEX and LME prices climbed briefly to six-month highs on Tuesday after a further dip in LME stocks to 6-1/4-year lows. Demand in the U.S. was healthy, traders said.
There was some concern over tightness in the LME December contract, especially around December 13, which traders said related to Sumitomo's announcement of huge losses on June 13 in New York.

Those who immediately sold LME three-months after the announcement later took metal out of warehouses from September 13, when the shorts were able to roll forward another three-months into the contango to December 13, brokers said.
Remaining shorts were now being squeezed by low inventory, higher prices and yawning LME backwardation.

With spot LME now higher than its COMEX counterpart - 109.6 to 108.2 cents respectively at close on Tuesday - traders said the build-up at COMEX's Baltimore depot could slow down and metal may be diverted to the LME's depot in the same city.
LME Long Beach stocks may also reverse their long decline and begin increasing, traders added.
"There will be some confusion about warehouse movements. Baltimore is hilarious," a physical trader said.

A persistent LME premium over COMEX could also divert metal to Europe - probably for outright sales rather than into warehouses - which might otherwise have come to the U.S., an East Coast brass mill official said.
U.S copper premiums remained at 2.75 to 3.00 cents per pound over spot COMEX.
COMEX stocks are historically high at over 40,000 short tons, but are unlikely to move significantly higher because of the spot LME premium over COMEX, traders said.

U.S cathode production should rise in the first quarter of next year when Kennecott Utah Copper was expected to reach its full design capacity of 310,000 short tons a year, up from about 75 percent of capacity at the start of the present quarter.
And higher copper prices should also help ease cathode demand by luring more scrap from the woodwork, though offtake was due to weaken slightly until the next quarter.

Many people now wanted to sell material or price open contracts on the back of higher prices, in stark contrast to the market tightness over the summer due to weaker cathode prices, a Midwest scrap merchant said.
"But most of the mills are going to lose two production days this month, and as many as five to ten days in December due to seasonal holidays," the merchant added.
Nevertheless, there could still be a labor dispute at Phelps Dodge's Chino mine in New Mexico where workers have been without contracts since June 30.
